This image is a stacked histogram that illustrates the distribution of monthly funding across various regions, measured in millions of U.S. dollars. The chart is titled "Distribution of Monthly Funding Across Regions," with the x-axis labeled "Monthly Funding (Millions USD)" and the y-axis labeled "Number of Projects."

The histogram is divided into twelve bins, each representing a specific range of monthly funding amounts. The data is color-coded by region, with each color representing a different area: Metro North (pink), Metro South (brown), Suburban East (green), Rural West (teal), Metro Central (light blue), Suburban North (dark blue), and Rural North (purple).

At the lower end of the funding spectrum, around 0.7 to 1.0 million USD, the number of projects is relatively low, with contributions primarily from Metro South, Rural West, and Suburban East. As funding increases to approximately 1.0 to 1.5 million USD, the number of projects grows, showing contributions from all regions, with noticeable stacks from Metro North, Suburban East, Metro Central, and Rural North.

In the mid-range of 1.5 to 2.0 million USD, there is a significant number of projects, with the highest concentration around 1.5 million USD. This range shows substantial contributions mainly from Metro North, Suburban East, and Metro Central. Another peak appears around 2.0 to 2.3 million USD, predominantly featuring projects from Metro North and Metro Central.

In the higher funding ranges of 2.3 to 3.0 million USD, the number of projects decreases. The bins show fewer projects, with Metro North and Rural West having some presence. The highest funding bin, around 3.0 million USD, includes only a few projects, specifically from Metro North and Metro Central.

Overall, the chart reveals that most projects receive funding in the range of 1.0 to 2.0 million USD, with a diverse representation from all regions, while fewer projects receive either very low or very high monthly funding amounts.

args.message:
The defect was the y-axis label. It read "Average Approval Rate (%)", but the bars are project counts and summary.txt names the axis "Number of Projects". I changed only that label in chart.py and re-ran the script to regenerate output.png.

Verified on the figure object: the y-label is now "Number of Projects". The title ("Distribution of Monthly Funding Across Regions") and x-label ("Monthly Funding (Millions USD)") are unchanged. The rendered image shows the same 12-bin stacked histogram as before, with no overlapping or clipped text.

One thing I deliberately left alone: the chart has no legend (`legend=False`), so a reader cannot tell which colour is which region, even though the summary describes the bars as colour-coded by region. That argument may also have been introduced in error, but I wasn't certain enough to change it.

The defect was the y-axis label. It read "Average Approval Rate (%)", but the bars are project counts and summary.txt names the axis "Number of Projects". I changed only that label in chart.py and re-ran the script to regenerate output.png.

Verified on the figure object: the y-label is now "Number of Projects". The title ("Distribution of Monthly Funding Across Regions") and x-label ("Monthly Funding (Millions USD)") are unchanged. The rendered image shows the same 12-bin stacked histogram as before, with no overlapping or clipped text.

One thing I deliberately left alone: the chart has no legend (`legend=False`), so a reader cannot tell which colour is which region, even though the summary describes the bars as colour-coded by region. That argument may also have been introduced in error, but I wasn't certain enough to change it.
